note: Shared truth for swipe-to-reply on a message row. `dx` / `dy` are the gesture's travel from where the finger went down, in the platform's logical units (logical pixels on Flutter, points on SwiftUI, dp on Compose), signed: a positive `dx` moves towards the trailing edge of a left-to-right layout. Each kit implements one pure function over this table and the list draws the row `travel` away from its resting place while the finger is down, raising the swipe-reply intent on release only when `armed`. The rules these cases encode: only the leading direction counts, mirrored under RTL; the list's own vertical scrolling wins any drag whose horizontal travel is not at least 1.25 times its vertical travel; the row follows the finger as far as 56, then resists at 0.35 and never travels past 72; and 56 is where the gesture arms, so the reply affordance must be fully drawn at exactly that distance and not before. Compare `travel` with a tolerance of 0.001, because the resistance is floating point. Vue has no swipe — `MessageList.swipeReply` is registered for flutter, ios and compose only — because the web timeline is pointer-first and a horizontal touch drag there fights the list's own scrolling.
